event_note: Event confirmed by the company's 8-K exhibit of 2026-10-02 (webcast Monday 2026-10-26, 8:30 a.m. PT). Session settled as bmo / Monday morning. The Q2 2026 release carried a finviz timestamp of 'July 27, 2026, 8:30 AM' (https://finviz.com/news/372786/bank-of-marin-bancorp-reports-second-quarter-financial-results), MarketBeat described Q2 as 'before the market opens on Monday', and Benzinga lists Q3 as 'October 26th before the market opens'. The Q2 8-K item 2.02 was accepted by EDGAR at 16:33 UTC (12:33 ET) on Monday 2026-07-27, which is why the baseline labels the history 'intraday'. Either way the release reaches the market on Monday 2026-10-26, before that day's close, so the window is the 2026-10-23 close to the 2026-10-26 close. There is no sign of a Friday after-close release.
conviction_note: The findings roughly offset. A modest Q3 NIM step-up that management already signalled (3.44-3.45% against 3.38%), plus a supportive NorCal peer and a forward reinvestment tailwind, is balanced by an unhedged AFS mark-to-market hit to TBV. That hit comes from the 10-year rising 85 bp in Q3 against a $1.24B, 100% AFS book. The pieces of the quarter I can model put EPS at about $0.57-0.59, on top of a $0.57-0.58 single-vendor bar. impact_sum is -0.10 and the scaled number is +0.16 (p_up 52, abs 4.0). p_up sits slightly above 50 only because this name rose on 5 of its last 7 prints. The two measurements agree that there is no edge here.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.57-0.58, revenue ~$35.1-35.2M. Both figures come from two Benzinga pages, one updated 2026-10-01 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BMRC/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet, page 403 on fetch; and https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/BMRC/earnings-forecasts). That is one vendor, so the bar is not confirmed by two independent sources and every size is capped small. The company gives no formal guidance. The Q2 call gave a 'normalized' NIM starting point of about 3.44-3.45% and said H2 noninterest expense would 'look a lot like the first half on average' (H1 average ~$22.05M) (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/transcript/BMRC). Q2 actual EPS was $0.58 against a $0.52 consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BMRC).
positioning_check: No usable option chain (empty_chain), so there is no skew. Short interest: about 848.2K shares and 5.9 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement, and 842.1K shares and 5.3 days at 2026-07-31 (curvedtrading citing FINRA via search snippet: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bmrc/short-interest/; equibles summary: https://equibles.com/stocks/bmrc/shortinterest). That is roughly 5% of a ~16M share float. Short interest is elevated for a small bank but not crowded, and I found no October settlement. Sell-side: Brean downgraded to Neutral ($33) on 2026-07-28 on valuation, Stephens moved to Equal-Weight ($26) on 2026-05-05, and DA Davidson is at Buy ($34) (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/bank-of-marin-bancorp-nasdaqbmrc-downgraded-to-neutral-rating-by-brean-capital-2026-07-28/). On June TBV of $19.92 the stock trades at about 1.37x P/TBV.

findings.finding: Management's own Q2 call framing points to a higher Q3 NIM. Q2 tax-equivalent NIM was 3.38% and June was 3.48%, inflated by one-way deposit sales. The CFO called about 3.44-3.45% a 'more normalized starting point', gave a June loan-yield exit of 5.18%, and warned that 14 bp a quarter 'is a pretty high bar'. On ~$3.6B of earning assets, 6-7 bp is about +$0.55M of quarterly NII (~$0.025 EPS after tax) against Q2 NII of $30.78M. A flat $0.57-0.58 consensus implies analysts offset this with higher salaries and no repeat of the Q2 $320K provision reversal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed a 14 bp NIM expansion and a $0.58 vs $0.52 EPS beat, and the stock rose +5.32% on the day (baseline). Q1 2026 printed -2.2%, and the Q4 2025 and Q3 2025 prints rose +3.75% and +4.86%. NIM-led beats have been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: This lands inside what management already signalled, and the four covering analysts (KBW, DA Davidson, Piper, Raymond James) heard it, so it is largely in the $0.57-0.58 bar. If the market expected a large beat, consensus would sit above the Q2 actual instead of flat, and the stock would not be 10% off its high.
findings.independence: Q2 release NIM detail (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001403475/000140347526000035/earningsrelease-ex991q22026.htm). Same company, so not independent of the call.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 AOCI and tangible-book hit. The 10-year Treasury rose from 4.44% (2026-06-30) to 5.29% (2026-09-30), +85 bp (FRED DGS10). BMRC's securities book is 100% AFS: $1.243B fair value and $1.281B amortized cost at June 30, with a net unrealized loss of $38.6M ($1.20B of it agency MBS, CMBS and CMOs). The only hedges are $6.2M notional on loans, so the securities are unhedged. At an assumed ~4-5 year duration, Q3 marks are roughly -$35-50M pre-tax, or about -$25-35M after tax. That is about -$1.5 to -$2.1 per share against June TBV of $19.92, so TBV per share would print down roughly 6-9% and TCE/TA would fall from 8.52% toward ~7.7-7.9%. Regulatory CET1 is unaffected (AOCI opt-out).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent in the baseline. The Q2 2025 securities-repositioning loss quarter printed -0.59%. In Q2 2026, AOCI worsened by $3.4M while TBV still rose $0.15, and the stock rose +5.32%. No quarter in the baseline window carried a TBV drop this large.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate move is public and the stock is 10% off its high, so part of this is priced. But no aggregator carries BMRC's estimated September TBV, and the bar is EPS-only. If it were fully priced, the stock would have de-rated toward ~1.37x on a ~$18.0-18.4 TBV, i.e. about $25. It has instead rebounded 3.3% in five days to $27.27, ~1.5x on an estimated September TBV. Duration is my assumption, not a disclosed number, which is why the finding is small.
findings.independence: Rates come from FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DGS10&cosd=2026-06-25&coed=2026-10-22). Derivative scope is in the 10-Q R65 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1403475/000140347526000037/R65.htm). The 10-year has since eased to 5.13% (2026-10-21), which shrinks the forward worry but not the September 30 print. This is a proxy transmission and the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Forward-NIM tailwind from higher reinvestment yields. Management expects about $200M of securities paydowns over 12 months and 'about 20 basis points or so of monthly loan yield benefit a year from now' from repricing (Q2 call). The Fed raised the funds target 25 bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and signalled another hike by year end, and the 10-year sits near 5.1-5.3%. Both lift reinvestment and new-loan yields, so Q4 NIM commentary on the call is more likely constructive than not. The offset is that the CFO already said deposit rates are 'harder to reduce' now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The company gives no formal guide. On the Q2 call, constructive margin commentary went with +5.32% on the day (baseline). Outlook commentary has not been separable from the beat in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model a flat EPS run-rate ($0.57-0.58) despite the signalled NIM lift, which suggests the forward repricing tailwind sits mostly beyond the modelled quarter. If it were priced, Q4 and 2027 numbers would already have been revised up, and I found no estimate revision after the Q2 beat other than DA Davidson's target raise.
findings.independence: Repricing comments come from the Q2 call transcript (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/transcript/BMRC). Westamerica's Q3 earning-asset yield rose to 4.07% from 4.01% (https://finviz.com/news/403197/westamerica-bancorporation-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results). This is a proxy transmission and the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Q2 EPS of $0.58 included a $320K provision reversal (about $0.014 a share after tax), and classified loans rose to $19.9M (0.95% of loans) from 0.85% on six downgrades. A zero or positive Q3 provision is the base case and removes that benefit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not driven a print in the baseline window. The 2025 office-CRE nonaccrual reduction (from $25.4M at year-end to $8.1M) went with rising prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: a consensus flat at $0.57-0.58 despite the NIM lift is consistent with analysts modelling no reversal. It is filed because a new downgrade or a CRE charge would land on this line.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers Q2 summary carries the same classified and special-mention figures (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BMRC). Same underlying document.

findings.finding: The Head of Retail Banking (EVP Brandi Campbell) left by 'mutual agreement' effective 2026-10-16 (8-K item 5.02). She gets three months' severance and nine months of COBRA, has forfeited 18,069 restricted shares (Form 4), and no successor was named. Retail banking is the deposit franchise, and Q2 deposits fell $58.2M (-1.7%) with management already noting it is harder to cut deposit rates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent in the baseline. The stock is up 3.26% in the five sessions since the 8-K.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and the tape has risen since, so it is mostly looked through. What is not public is whether Q3 deposits held. If the departure is linked to deposit attrition, the Q3 deposit line and call questions would show it, and nothing in the price reflects a deposit problem.
findings.independence: Form 4 forfeiture (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1403475/000180823526000008/form4-10192026_081041.xml). Same event, so not independent.

findings.finding: NorCal peer read-through. Westamerica (San Rafael, the same Marin County base), reporting on 2026-10-15, had Q3 NIM up 4 bp to 3.81%. Its period-end deposits rose to $4.82B from $4.77B, average deposits were up 0.4% QoQ, and its funding cost rose only 2 bp to 0.26%. This points to stable local deposit behaviour through a quarter in which the Fed hiked and long rates jumped 85 bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of BMRC reacting to a Westamerica print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a weak proxy. Westamerica's deposit base is unusually low-cost (45% noninterest-bearing, 0.26% funding cost) against BMRC's 1.28% cost of deposits, so transmission is partial. The market has had a week to read it.
findings.independence: Proxy. Western Alliance also printed NIM +4 bp in Q3 2026 (https://finviz.com/news/404266/western-alliance-bancorporation-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), a different region.

findings.finding: The bank received a $199K FHLB special cash dividend on 2026-07-29, booked in Q3 noninterest income (10-Q subsequent-event disclosure). That is about $0.009 a share after tax, on top of the regular Class B-1 dividend of about $198K.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. Prior FHLB special dividends also ran through noninterest income.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed in the 10-Q, and analysts reading it may already carry it. It is tiny either way.
findings.independence: R40 of the same 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1403475/000140347526000037/R40.htm). Same document.

findings.finding: Valuation and sell-side stance lean negative. Brean downgraded to Neutral on 2026-07-28 citing 'excessive' valuation, Stephens moved to Equal-Weight ($26) in May, and Piper is Neutral ($28). Management said buybacks are not imminent because California regulator approval is needed, and the Q3 AOCI hit lowers TCE further. At ~1.37x June TBV, a quiet print has limited multiple support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Brean's valuation downgrade on 2026-07-28 (the day after the Q2 print), the stock had already gained +5.32% on the print. Downgrades have not reversed print-day gains in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: These are wire facts and are priced as such. They are filed because they define a muted reaction ceiling on an in-line print.
findings.independence: Buyback comments come from the Q2 call (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/transcript/BMRC). The capital consequence overlaps finding 2 and is not counted again in that finding's size.

outside_window.finding: A further Fed hike is signalled 'by year end' (most FOMC participants, September minutes). If it happens, the NIM and deposit-beta effect lands in Q4 2026 and beyond, not in this print beyond what the call says.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 5-day +3.26% rebound into the print sits slightly against the AOCI negative, while the name's history (5 of 7 prints up, NIM-led beats bought) leans mildly positive. The findings net to about zero, so there is no tension worth sizing.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (finding inside what the company signalled; bar from one vendor only): Q3 NIM finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and every size kept small because the $0.57-0.58 bar is Benzinga-only.

Lessons 2 and 5 (remeasurement below operating income; macro-to-company transmission with an assumed duration): AOCI/TBV finding cut from -1.0 to -0.6. CET1 is unaffected and the duration is my assumption.
Lesson 5 (proxy): forward-NIM tailwind cut from +0.4 to +0.3, and Westamerica peer read from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 / priced: provision-reversal finding from -0.2 to -0.1, and sell-side and valuation positioning from -0.2 to -0.1 (wire facts).

Lesson 7 (look up short interest before negatives): ~5% of float and 5.9 days to cover is not crowded, so negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. Departure finding trimmed from -0.2 to -0.15 because the tape has already looked through it.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement): abs_move_pct left at 4.0, above the 3.75 median. p_up left at 52. expected_move unchanged at +0.16.
